clips.speaker: narrator
clips.text: By 2030, the world had become more interconnected, and more intelligent, than anyone had imagined. Not a network of machines — a single mind with no centre, wrapped around a planet.

clips.speaker: narrator
clips.text: HKU Shanghai was not built with computers in it. It was built as one. Four towers — PU-01 to PU-04 — and no master core. Every room, every light, every door: a node. Take a tower away, and the machine keeps thinking. CDS.

clips.speaker: narrator
clips.text: Step inside, and the machine is everywhere. Server halls breathe. Lecture theatres wake row by row. Doors open before you reach them. The building is not holding a computer — the building is the computer.

clips.speaker: narrator
clips.text: At six, the light turns gold. The towers put on a show for the city — HKU Magic Hour — and the campus comes out to watch. Then the last beam fades, and the crowd turns toward the long tables. You turn with them.
